title: Elastic orthorhombic anisotropic full-waveform inversion using the scattering-integral approach based on the tensor-train decomposition

authors.name: J.-W. Oh
authors.affiliation: Chonbuk National University, Korea

authors.name: T. Alkhalifah
authors.affiliation: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Saudi Arabia

abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) for elastic orthorhombic anisotropic media is computationally expensive and requires careful parameterization. We develop an efficient multiparameter FWI approach using the scattering-integral method with the tensor-train (TT) decomposition to reduce the computational cost of building sensitivity kernels. The TT decomposition compresses the Green's function tensor, enabling efficient computation of the partial derivative wavefields without explicitly solving additional wave equations for each parameter perturbation. We demonstrate the method on synthetic examples and analyze the trade-offs between orthorhombic parameters.

title: Overview of graphite supply chain and its challenges

authors.name: J. Park
authors.affiliation: Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM), Daejeon, South Korea

abstract: Graphite is a critical mineral for the clean energy transition, particularly as the primary anode material in lithium-ion batteries. However, its supply chain faces significant risks due to the high concentration of production and processing in China, low market value, and geopolitical uncertainties. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the graphite supply chain, from mining to battery anode material production, covering both natural and synthetic graphite pathways. Key challenges including environmental impacts, supply chain concentration, and trade policy risks are discussed. Five strategic recommendations are proposed: expanded exploration, advanced mining technologies, cost-effective small-deposit mining, enhanced government support, and standardized HS codes for material tracking.

title: Mono-component acoustic VTI full-waveform inversion using the displacement wavefields

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University, South Korea

authors.name: J.-W. Oh
authors.affiliation: Chonbuk National University, South Korea

authors.name: D.-J. Min
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University, South Korea

abstract: In acoustic full-waveform inversion (FWI) for VTI media, the radiation patterns of the partial derivative wavefields for the mono-component virtual sources are inconsistent with those from the elastic scattering theory. To overcome this limitation, we propose using vector wavefields by converting the mono-component pressure wavefields into displacement components based on the equation of motion. The proposed method yields radiation patterns and sensitivity kernels similar to those of the coupled wave equation with lower computational costs. We demonstrate through numerical examples using a simple syncline model and the modified Marmousi-II model with borehole acquisition that the proposed method properly updates the anisotropic parameters by the correct gradient direction consistent with the elastic scattering theory.

title: Pseudo-acoustic reverse-time migration for 2D VTI media using the Volve OBC data

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University / KIGAM, South Korea

authors.name: J.-W. Oh
authors.affiliation: Chonbuk National University, South Korea

authors.name: D.-J. Min
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University, South Korea

abstract: We examine the feasibility of mono-component-based pseudo-acoustic reverse-time migration (PA-RTM) for 2D VTI media using real OBC data acquired in the Volve oil field of the North Sea. To investigate the influence of anisotropic parameters on the RTM image and the sensitivity of data components to seismic anisotropy, we first conducted RTM using synthetic data generated using anisotropic tomography models provided with the observed data. From these synthetic experiments, we confirmed that the anisotropic parameter delta is not a significant factor in PA-RTM for VTI media. Isotropic RTM using only pressure wavefield data located the reflectors poorly compared to anisotropic RTM. However, RTM with vertical acceleration was less affected by seismic anisotropy than that using pressure wavefield data due to the intrinsic properties of vertical acceleration data. Real data examples showed that PA-RTM for VTI media successfully located the target reflectors using either pressure wavefields or vertical acceleration data, and that vertical acceleration data were less influenced than pressure wavefield data by anisotropic properties.

abstract: We applied 3D electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) to explore the Yeoncheon titanium magnetite (TM) deposit in the Gonamsan igneous intrusion. This intrusion is classified as quartz monzodiorite (QMD) and monzogabbro-monzodiorite (GMD) according to the ratio of mafic rocks. Because iron-titanium mineralization is mainly developed in the GMD, separating the two monzodiorites provides helpful information for identifying ore deposits. The electrical resistivity survey was carried out along three parallel survey lines using dipole spacings of 20, 40, and 60 m. We performed 3D electrical resistivity inversion from 2D resistivity models to investigate the complex mountainous terrain. From the 3D inversion results, we were able to separate the region of the GMD based on the measured resistivity of the drilling data.

title: An efficient multiparameter acoustic anisotropic full-waveform inversion depending on parameterization

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University, South Korea

authors.name: J.-W. Oh
authors.affiliation: Chonbuk National University, South Korea

authors.name: D.-J. Min
authors.affiliation: Seoul National University, South Korea

abstract: We investigate the influence of parameterization on acoustic VTI full-waveform inversion using the decomposed equation with displacement wavefields. By comparing different parameterizations including (vp, epsilon, delta), (vph, eta, epsilon), and others, we analyze the trade-offs between model parameters through radiation pattern analysis and numerical FWI experiments. The decomposed equation with displacement wavefields provides efficient gradient computation while maintaining correct radiation patterns consistent with elastic scattering theory. We demonstrate that the choice of parameterization significantly affects the inversion results, especially for anisotropic parameters, and that certain parameterizations reduce trade-offs between parameters.

title: Rock classification in a vanadiferous titanomagnetite deposit based on supervised machine learning

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM), Daejeon, South Korea

authors.name: Seungwook Shin
authors.affiliation: Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM), Daejeon, South Korea

abstract: We applied supervised machine learning methods to classify rocks in the Gonamsan vanadiferous titanomagnetite deposit in Pocheon, South Korea. Using geophysical data including electrical resistivity, chargeability, and magnetic susceptibility from both rock samples and field measurements, we trained and compared five ML algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Deep Neural Network (DNN). The models classify rocks into three categories: ore-bearing monzogabbro-monzodiorite (GMD), host quartz monzodiorite (QMD), and metamorphic rock (ME). Among the tested algorithms, Random Forest showed the best overall performance with 95.7% accuracy. Feature importance analysis revealed that electrical resistivity is the most significant feature for distinguishing GMD from other rock types.

title: Two-Step Seismic Monitoring Strategy with Diffraction-Angle Filtering for Carbon Capture and Storage

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
abstract: We proposed a two-step seismic monitoring approach for carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects using diffraction-angle filtering (DAF). In the first step, a velocity model is constructed using FWI with mode IV of DAF. Mode IV of DAF helps to prevent the local minima problem because the gradient of FWI is mainly composed of low-wavenumber components. In the second step, the seismic image is obtained by RTM with mode V of DAF using the updated velocity model through FWI, and the boundaries between layers are well represented due to the high-wavenumber components. The behavior of CO2 can be monitored from the difference in seismic images between surveys performed before and after injection. We implemented synthetic testing using the velocity model in the Volve oil field.

title: BERT 기반 사전학습을 이용한 탄성파 자료처리: 송신원 모음 배열 비교

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

abstract: This study applies BERT-based pretraining to enhance the efficiency of seismic data processing and compares the performance of receiver array and time array arrangements. Experiments were conducted on synthetic seismic data including simple flat-layer velocity models with and without faults. The pretraining stage used masked input data to learn data reconstruction, followed by fine-tuning for denoising, velocity prediction, and fault detection tasks. Both receiver array and time array configurations showed similar denoising performance, but the time array outperformed in velocity prediction and fault detection tasks. The time array achieved perfect accuracy, recall, and F1 score of 1.00 in fault detection, while the receiver array recorded 0.82 accuracy. The BERT-based pretraining model with time arrays can more effectively capture spatial distributions and event patterns, making it suitable for seismic data processing tasks.

title: Domain Adaptation for Mineral Exploration Using Geophysical and Drilling Data

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

abstract: This study demonstrated the application of domain adaptation to bridge the gap between diverse geoscience datasets, enhancing mineral exploration. Models trained on detailed, labeled drilling data were adapted to interpret broader, unlabeled geophysical data, effectively maintaining predictive capabilities across different domains. The Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) model was chosen for its ability to effectively adapt features across domains without needing labeled data from the target domain. The model was evaluated using the silhouette score, which confirmed its effectiveness in clustering data. It performed well on test data from the source domain, successfully learning and adapting to the data characteristics. Although the borehole data from the target domain included only HOST labels, it was used to indirectly validate the model's predictive accuracy. The absence of overlap with areas classified as ORE by the trained model suggests it identified relevant geological features.

title: Cross-Attention-Enhanced U-Net for Elastic Wavefield Vector Decomposition in Anisotropic Media

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

abstract: This study presents a cross-attention enhanced U-Net architecture for elastic wavefield vector decomposition in anisotropic media. The method combines deep learning with a dual-branch encoder structure to process displacement components separately while maintaining their relationships through cross-attention mechanisms. The results show that the cross-attention mechanisms improve the decomposition quality, achieving better accuracy and fewer artifacts compared to conventional U-Net architectures. The mean PSNR increased from 42.8360 dB to 44.1008 dB and SSIM from 0.8897 to 0.9043 with cross-attention. The model's performance on larger domains and different geological settings, demonstrated through experiments with the BP and Hess VTI models, indicates its potential for practical seismic applications.

title: Elastic Wavefield Decomposition in VTI Media Using Tensor-Train Decomposition

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

abstract: This paper presents a tensor-train decomposition framework for elastic wavefield decomposition in VTI media. The proposed method formulates the Christoffel-based projection operator as a four-dimensional tensor and constructs its compressed TT representation using the TT-cross algorithm. The method includes a residual-orthogonal decomposition (ROD) strategy that extracts the qSV component from the residual wavefield after removing the qP component, reducing cross-talk between separated modes. The proposed TT method consistently improved separation fidelity across three 2D VTI tests (two-layer, BP 2007 subset, and Overthrust-based model). Reconstruction errors for TT remained below 1% (0.094-0.89%), whereas CUR showed larger errors (1.67-6.44%), yielding a 4-46x improvement, with markedly reduced cross-talk. The TT method also demonstrated favorable computational scaling for larger grids with GPU acceleration.

title: SeisMamba: A Dual-Axis State-Space Model for DAS Denoising and Phase Picking

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

abstract: SeisMamba is a hierarchical encoder-decoder (U-Net style) network for DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensing) data processing in which all sequence-modeling computations are performed by DualMamba blocks. The DualMamba block employs parallel channel-axis and time-axis BiMamba branches with learnable axis fusion, exploiting the anisotropic structure of DAS gathers. The network handles both denoising and phase picking tasks. Compared against ResUNet (CNN baseline) and SwinDAS (Swin Transformer), SeisMamba achieves the highest phase-picking accuracy (91.52%) on the DeepSubDAS real dataset, while ResUNet leads in denoising SNR (29.19 dB vs. 26.98 dB). SeisMamba outperforms ResUNet on colored noise by 0.61 dB (31.09 vs 30.48 dB) due to its global temporal context from bidirectional SSM scans. SeisMamba has 4.16M parameters with O(n) computational complexity, demonstrating favorable scalability for long DAS records.

title: Seismic Wave Propagation and Normal-Mode Analysis of Asteroid (99942) Apophis for the RAMSES Mission

authors.name: Youngjae Shin
authors.affiliation: Gyeongsang National University, Jinju, South Korea

journal: Manuscript (not yet published, target: The Planetary Science Journal)
abstract: This study presents the first three-dimensional continuum elastic wave propagation model for tidal seismic excitation of asteroid (99942) Apophis during its 2029 Earth flyby, computed with the spectral-element code SPECFEM3D on a voxel mesh of the asteroid's bi-lobed shape. A systematic parameter study spanning P-wave velocity Vp = 50-300 m/s, bulk density rho = 1500-3150 kg/m3, and quality factor Qmu = 20-100 reveals the following results: Tidal peak ground velocity ranges from 0.001 to 0.14 nm/s at the baseline model (Vp = 200 m/s), falling 7-1000 times below the SIA noise floor of 1 nm/s. The bi-lobed shape supports seven independently verified normal-mode eigenfrequencies at 0.35-1.07 Hz for the baseline model, confirmed as source-independent body resonances. Ground velocity scales as PGV proportional to Vp^-2 and inversely with density, while Qmu contributes less than 3.5% variation. A critical P-wave velocity for tidal detectability with the existing instrument is approximately 75 m/s, corresponding to the extreme low end of laboratory measurements for asteroid analogs.
